subject: Region pinning + transient replication for analytics/metrics
messages:
From: Luc Morel <luc@acme-retail.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: data-protection@acme-retail.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Region pinning + transient replication for analytics/metrics

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're lining up our procurement checklist: can Redwood commit to keeping customer inference and request-level logs strictly within the EU region for EU customers, while still allowing limited, transient replication of aggregated analytics/metrics to our global analytics cluster? Our use case is dashboards and ML feature pipelines that consume anonymized/aggregated telemetry (no raw request payloads) across regions for product analytics.

Specifically we need to understand:
- Whether Redwood can guarantee that raw request payloads and user-provided prompt inputs for EU customers never leave EU boundaries (including backups and logs) except as explicitly allowed.
- If any cross-region processing will occur by default (e.g., telemetry, observability, autoscaling traces) and whether those flows can be restricted or anonymized.
- List of subprocessors that might be involved in any non-EU processing (in particular US-based analytics or logging vendors).
- Whether Redwood is willing to sign a narrow DPA addendum that documents a region-pinning commitment and allowed exceptions for aggregated metrics.

We are leaning toward a model where inference and raw logs stay in EU, but aggregated metrics (counts, histograms, deltas) can be shared with TTL and aggregation rules. Can you confirm feasibility and share suggested wording? Also happy to schedule a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Luc
Head of Data Governance
Acme Retail

Attachments: none
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Luc Morel <luc@acme-retail.com>
Cc: data-protection@acme-retail.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region pinning + transient replication for analytics/metrics

Hi Luc — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: yes, we can support the pattern you describe, but there are a few configuration and contractual nuances I want to call out so we set expectations correctly.

High-level options we typically offer (we can pick one in the addendum):
- EU-only strict: inference, request logs, and backups remain in EU; no replication of telemetry off-EU.
- EU-primary + aggregated replication: raw inputs and request-level logs remain in EU; aggregated/anonymized metrics (e.g., counts/histograms with k-anonymity thresholds) can be replicated to other regions for dashboards and ML features. Replication is configurable and can be TTL-bound.
- EU with transient cache replication: allows short-lived KV/cache replication to other regions for latency-sensitive workloads (TTL typically <= 4 hours), but we do not persist raw prompt payloads in non-EU storage.

What we need from you to finalize the wording:
1) A definition of "PII/RAW_PAYLOAD" for this contract (examples you consider sensitive).
2) A maximum acceptable TTL for any transient replication (if you want to limit it beyond our default suggestions).
3) Whether aggregated metrics must meet an aggregation threshold (we can enforce a minimum bucket size).

Subprocessors: we use a mix of cloud infra and observability partners. I will circulate a subprocessors list but the DPA addendum will explicitly state which subprocessors may process aggregated metrics outside EU and which cannot touch raw payloads.

I've attached a preliminary region pin matrix (region_pin_matrix.xlsx) showing default routing and options — treat it as draft. If you'd like, I can loop in our legal ops for a one-page addendum draft and propose specific language around backups, logs, and cache replication.

Would you be available for a 30-min call on Monday to hash this out?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Product Operations — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: region_pin_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, stub)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Region pinning + transient replication for analytics/metrics

Folks — forwarding Acme's request. They want a contractual commitment that raw inputs and request-level logs for EU customers never leave EU, but are OK with aggregated/anonymized metrics being replicated to global analytics.

Ask list:
- Rishi: can you produce a one-page DPA addendum draft that includes the three option patterns (EU-only, EU-primary+aggregated replication, EU with transient cache) and a subprocessors appendix. We should include specific language on backups, retention, and emergency cross-region access.
- Laura: confirm whether the "transient cache replication" path (TTL <= 4 hours, no persistence) is implementable with current runtime and what telemetry traces might still transit non-EU (autoscaler metrics, eviction traces). Note any engineering caveats.
- Marissa: sales will need a short playbook and negotiation guidance (preferred default offer, allowed concessions like TTL upper bound, and what requires legal escalation).

I attached a draft matrix (region_pin_matrix.xlsx) and a redline template for the addendum (dpa-deployment-addendum.pdf). If we can get a draft back to Acme by EOD Monday that would keep momentum.

Thanks — Soojin

Attachments: region_pin_matrix.xlsx, dpa-deployment-addendum.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Luc Morel <luc@acme-retail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region pinning + transient replication for analytics/metrics — proposed commitments and next steps

Hi Luc — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal review, here's a concise proposal we can put in a DPA addendum; happy to adjust wording after your review.

Summary of commitments (proposed language):
- Region pinning: For EU-designated customers, Redwood will route inference requests, request-level logs, and backups to EU-based infrastructure and will not persist raw request payloads outside the EU except as explicitly allowed below.
- Allowed exception — aggregated metrics: Aggregated and anonymized metrics (counts, histograms, aggregated latency buckets) may be replicated to Redwood-hosted analytics clusters outside the EU for dashboards and non-identifying ML features. Aggregation must meet a minimum anonymity threshold and may be configured by the customer.
- Allowed exception — transient cache replication: For latency-sensitive workloads, Redwood may perform short-lived KV/cache replication to non-EU regions with a maximum TTL configurable per-customer (default proposed: 4 hours). Raw prompt inputs will not be persisted in non-EU storage as part of this flow.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and will mark those authorized for aggregated-metrics processing outside the EU. Any change to subprocessors impacting raw payload processing will require advance notice and a mitigation plan.

Attachments and links: I attached the draft DPA addendum (dpa-deployment-addendum.pdf) and the region routing matrix (region_pin_matrix.xlsx). I've also shared a read-only drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/acme-deployment/region-pin-matrix.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Please confirm which option you prefer (EU-only | EU-primary+aggregated replication | EU with transient cache + TTL).
2) If you pick "aggregated replication", provide your desired anonymity threshold and max TTL for metrics.
3) Our legal team will issue a one-page addendum (attached draft) and list of subprocessors; we aim to get the signed addendum within two weeks once language is agreed.
4) Optional: 30-min call to finalize operational definitions (PII vs aggregated metric).

We will not route raw customer prompt payloads outside the EU in the default configuration. If you have any specific regulatory constraints (e.g., blocking certain cloud vendors), flag them and we'll surface them to ops/legal.

If that reads OK, reply with the option you want and any thresholds you need and we'll move the addendum forward.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Product Operations — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa-deployment-addendum.pdf (draft addendum), region_pin_matrix.xlsx (routing draft)
